The test image shows a whole banana plant where the main pseudostem appears dead/collapsed (brown, dry, splitting at the base), with dried collapsed leaves surrounding it and young green suckers emerging from the base. This pattern strongly suggests a vascular wilt disease.

Now I'll read one reference image from my top candidate — Panama Disease (stem view, since the pseudostem collapse is the key feature):

The Panama Disease reference stem image shows characteristic splitting of the pseudostem with yellow-orange tissue and dark vascular discoloration streaks.

**Comparison to test image:**
- Test image: Dead main plant with collapsed/dried pseudostem at the base, all leaves dried and hanging, young suckers emerging — classic whole-plant collapse from vascular wilt
- Panama Disease description: "Splitting of the base of the pseudostem", "collapsed leaves hang down the pseudostem like a skirt", plant death with suckers emerging from infected corm
- The pattern matches perfectly: complete plant death from soil-borne vascular wilt, pseudostem splitting, and the emergence of suckers from what appears to be a killed parent plant

No other candidate fits: leaf spot diseases (Cordana, Sigatoka) would show spotted but otherwise alive leaves; Bunchy_Top would show bunched stunted leaves at the crown; Anthracnose/Cigar_End_Rot affect fruit/pods.
